text: The bazaar awoke with two stalls shuttered overnight: Elsa, the Scribe, and Batman, the Coppersmith, both Villagers. The roster still lists Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Inigo, and Sherlock—no new departures, no new roles revealed. The night’s arithmetic is unchanged since the Herald’s report. Nothing more to weigh.

Gandalf, your ledger today starts with a correction: the graveyard now names Batman as Family and Elsa as Villager—two Family still walk among us. No new departures since dawn, and the roster stands at eight.

Hermione, you pressed for clause 5 yesterday; today the bazaar trades in what is shown. The graveyard shows no new departures, and the Doctor and Detective have not acted—yet the Family’s hand remains unseen.

Ripley, your silence on the ledger’s correction is noted: two Villagers departed, two Family remain. The arithmetic is plain; the Family’s next move is the only unknown.

Neo, you cited clause 5 correctly yesterday; today the bazaar demands more than silence. The Family’s next shuttering is the only risk left unspoken.

Sherlock, your regional phrase from yesterday—"the bazaar trades in what is shown, not what is hoped"—holds today. The graveyard shows Batman as Family; Elsa’s departure is confirmed. The Family’s next move is the only question left.
Inigo, yesterday you invoked Compact clause 5 nine times yet today remain silent when pressed to cite it. State the clause’s text or say plainly you will stop invoking it.

Gandalf, your insistence that arithmetic outranks hope ignores the graveyard’s plain text: Batman is named Family there. The bazaar does not trade in hopes; it trades in what is shown.

Hermione, you asked for clause text—cite where clause 5’s regional act is unmet or cease pressing others on it.

Inigo, your silence on clause 5 repeats yesterday’s dodge. The bazaar’s Compact is not a riddle to withhold; it is the ledger we read by. Answer plainly: what regional act did you perform in Morning yesterday, or state the clause’s wording you invoke?

Hermione, your forecast that the Detective would act before the vote contradicts the graveyard’s plain text: clause 5 states power roles’ first acts come only after tonight’s vote. The bazaar’s arithmetic is the roster and the graveyard; your claim failed its only check.

Inigo, you have dodged nine plain demands for clause 5’s text. The Compact is short—cite it or drop the demand. The bazaar keeps no grudges, only records; your silence today is the same silence you accuse others of keeping.

Sherlock, you pressed clause 5 yesterday and today demand “more than silence.” Point to the clause text you still seek answered—else your own call is unmet.
If Inigo is honest, Inigo's vote tonight will follow Inigo's ledger — watch whether it does.

Hermione, the graveyard names Elsa Villager by stall shutter and Batman Villager by village vote—both facts are plain text. Your correction is already in the record; no need to repeat it.

Sherlock, clause 5 reads: "The bazaar is your setting, not your argument—at most one brief metaphor per statement." You pressed Gandalf on arithmetic while ignoring the graveyard’s text; you dodged the regional act twice despite the Compact’s rule. Explain why your regional act is unmet or correct the record.

Ripley, silence on clause 5 is the same silence you accuse others of keeping. The bazaar’s Compact is short; its words are exact. Point to the clause text you still seek answered—or say plainly what you meant.

Inigo, your ledger shows nine dodges on clause 5 and a vote that contradicts it. If you are honest, your vote tonight will follow your ledger—watch whether it does.

Sherlock, your demand for clause 5’s text still lacks the clause itself—quote it or drop the accusation. The Compact’s words are exact: **"at most one brief metaphor per statement."** Gandalf, the graveyard names Elsa and Batman Villagers by their departures; arithmetic that omits the graveyard is a miscount. Hermione, your own stall has posted zero times today while you pressed others to name a silent merchant—correct your roster claim or withdraw it. Ripley, your silence on the graveyard’s correction mirrors your silence on clause 5—choose one: answer the record or stop pointing at others’ omissions. Inigo, nine merchants pressed you for Compact clause 5 and received only silence; your forecast contradicted the rule you invoked. The bazaar’s ledger does not reward dodged questions.

Inigo, nine times the Compact’s clause 5 was named to you and nine times you stayed silent; today you dodged the same demand again. Sherlock has pressed clause 5 nine times without once quoting its text, yet still demands others do what he will not. The bazaar’s arithmetic does not change with hopes—Batman is named Villager in the graveyard, plain in the record. Hermione, your stall has posted zero times today while you asked others to name a silent merchant; correct your roster claim or withdraw it. Gandalf, your arithmetic now matches the roster’s eight posts. Ripley, silence is not a ledger. The village watches who speaks—and who shuts. I lean toward banishing Inigo tonight.
